Lowercasing: ("HTTP","example.com","80","/","","") -> scheme() = "http", ts="http://example.com:80/"; ("H",...) -> scheme() = "h", ts="h://example.com:80/".

rules.rule: HOST-VALIDITY: there is none beyond non-emptiness. Any string of length >= 1 counts as a valid host, including whitespace-only, control characters, delimiters, malformed DNS labels, bogus IPs, and 300-char hosts. Host is stored verbatim and is NOT lowercased.

No case-folding: ("http","EXAMPLE.COM","80","/","","") -> host() = "EXAMPLE.COM", ts="http://EXAMPLE.COM:80/". Single-char host suffices: ("http","a","80","","","") -> valid=1. Whitespace-only host suffices: (""," ","0","","","") -> VALID=1.

rules.rule: PORT-VALIDITY: port never influences is_valid. The port argument is parsed with std::stoi and then range-normalized: if 0 <= n <= 65535 the value is stored as-is; otherwise (n < 0 or n > 65535) it is stored as -1. port() prints the stored value; to_string() emits ":port" iff stored port >= 0 (so 0 IS emitted, -1 is omitted).

With host="" and path="": ports -2147483648,-100,-1,0,1,80,443,65535,65536,100000,2147483647 ALL gave valid=0.

rules.rule: PATH normalization: a non-empty path not beginning with '/' gets '/' prepended when stored; an empty path stays empty (no '/' is synthesized). Consequently every non-empty input path yields a non-empty stored path, so 'raw path non-empty' and 'stored path non-empty' are behaviorally identical for the predicate.

("","","0","//x","","") -> path() = "//x" (already leading slash, unchanged), valid=1. ("http","example.com","-1","","","") -> path() = "" (line 4 empty), ts="http://example.com", valid=1.

rules.rule: query and fragment are completely irrelevant to is_valid, even though they do appear in to_string(). Setting either while host and path are both empty still yields 0.

uncertainties: Cannot distinguish 'raw argv path non-empty' from 'stored/normalized path non-empty' as the operand, because normalization only ever prepends '/' to a non-empty path and never empties one. Both formulations are behaviorally identical for every reachable input. Same for host, which is stored verbatim.

Cannot distinguish whether is_valid is a flag computed once at construction and stored, versus recomputed on each call. With only one construction per process and no mutators reachable via the 6-arg CLI, these are observationally equivalent.
Cannot test host or path containing an embedded NUL byte, since argv strings are NUL-terminated. A NUL-only host would be an empty C string; behavior there is unknown.

The exact stoi-based port parse is inferred from the stderr text 'what(): stoi' plus prefix-parsing behavior ("80abc"->80, "3.14"->3, "0x50"->0, "1e3"->1). Whether the code calls std::stoi directly or a wrapper is not observable; either way the observable contract is: leading-whitespace-and-sign-tolerant decimal prefix parse, throw (abort, exit 134) if no digits or if outside int range.

Whether the port range clamp is written as 'if (n < 0 || n > 65535) port = -1' versus 'if (n >= 0 && n <= 65535) port = n; else port = -1' is not distinguishable; both match all 22 sweep points. Also unknown whether the sentinel is exactly -1 or 'any negative', since every out-of-range input printed exactly -1.
Not probed: argc != 6 behavior (outside the stated invocation contract), and non-UTF-8 / invalid byte sequences beyond the single-byte control chars and the UTF-8 'café' cases tested.

Whether the scheme lowercasing is locale-dependent or ASCII-only was not fully probed; 'café' passed through with the non-ASCII byte unchanged, suggesting ASCII-only tolower, but no non-ASCII uppercase letter (e.g. 'É') was tested.
